lesson.title: Kubernetes from Zero, part 13: Volumes, PersistentVolumes, claims and StorageClasses
lesson.description: Keep data when Pods die: emptyDir, PersistentVolumeClaims, StorageClasses and dynamic provisioning, access modes and reclaim policies, tested on kind.
lesson.tested: Every command ran on a three-node kind v0.33.0 cluster (node v1.37.0, kubectl v1.37.2) on 10 Nov 2026
lesson.rule: A Pod asks for storage with a PersistentVolumeClaim; a StorageClass makes the PersistentVolume. Check the reclaim policy before you delete a claim.

cheatsheet.intro: emptyDir, claims, classes, and the commands from Lesson 13.

rows.name: emptyDir
rows.role: Scratch shared by the Pod's containers. It disappears with the Pod. Avoid hostPath. `medium: Memory` counts against memory.

rows.name: Claim
rows.role: A PersistentVolumeClaim is your request. The Pod names the claim and never names the volume.

rows.name: PersistentVolume
rows.role: The storage a claim binds to, one to one.

rows.name: StorageClass
rows.role: Names a provisioner and creates volumes on demand. kind's local-path class is the usual default.

rows.name: First consumer
rows.role: WaitForFirstConsumer: the claim stays Pending until a Pod uses it, so the volume can land on the Pod's node.

rows.name: ReadWriteOnce
rows.role: Pods on that one node can share the volume.

rows.name: ReadWriteMany
rows.role: Many nodes. Needs a driver that supports it. kind's local-path does not.

rows.name: ReadWriteOncePod
rows.role: Exactly one Pod. CSI volumes only.

rows.name: Delete / Retain
rows.role: Delete takes the storage with the claim. Retain leaves a Released PV and the bytes.
rows.where: check RECLAIM POLICY before you delete

commands.note: PVCs are namespaced, PVs are not
read the Events when a claim stays Pending
none on a stock kind cluster

homework.intro: Use the three-node kind cluster from part 3 and the namespace `k8s-from-zero`. The lesson's cluster is `k8s-ep13`, so node names on yours will differ. Answers are in the separate answer key.

sections.title: Recall
sections.hint: Answer from memory, then check the lesson.

exercises.q: What happens to an emptyDir when the Pod is deleted?
exercises.a: It disappears with the Pod. It is scratch space. The lesson says to avoid hostPath.

exercises.q: Which object does a Pod name, and which object is cluster-scoped?
exercises.a: The Pod names a PersistentVolumeClaim. The PersistentVolume is cluster-scoped and binds one to one. The Pod never names the PV.

exercises.q: What do RWO, RWX and RWOP mean in the lesson, and which ones does kind's local-path driver support?
exercises.a: ReadWriteOnce is one node. ReadWriteMany is many nodes. ReadWriteOncePod is one Pod, CSI only. The lab's provisioner said NodePath only supports ReadWriteOnce and ReadWriteOncePod.

exercises.q: What do the two reclaim policies do?
exercises.a: Delete takes the storage with the claim. It is the default for dynamic volumes. Retain leaves a Released PV and the bytes, for someone to clean up.

sections.title: Predict the outcome
sections.hint: Write your prediction first. Then check the answer key.

exercises.q: A new claim stays Pending and no Pod uses it yet. The class uses WaitForFirstConsumer. Is that a failure?
exercises.a: No. That is normal until a Pod uses it. If a Pod exists and the claim is still Pending, read the claim's events with `kubectl describe pvc`.

exercises.q: You ask kind for ReadWriteMany. What stays Pending, and where is the error?
exercises.a: The claim and the Pod both stay Pending. The claim's events say NodePath only supports ReadWriteOnce and ReadWriteOncePod. The Pod's own events can be empty, so read the claim.

exercises.q: A claim with `storageClassName: fast` stays Pending. What is missing?
exercises.a: No StorageClass named fast. The event says `storageclass.storage.k8s.io "fast" not found`. Check `kubectl get storageclass`.

exercises.q: You delete a claim and the data is still there. What policy did the volume have?
exercises.a: Retain. The PV becomes Released and the bytes stay until someone cleans them up. Check RECLAIM POLICY before you delete a claim.
